title: Investigate and remediate control-plane heartbeat flaps after Private VPC upgrade
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During the March 9th private/VPC control-plane upgrade (private-2026.03), multiple customer clusters experienced intermittent control-plane heartbeat failures and transient egress DNS resolution errors causing API timeouts and reconnect storms for private deployments. Impact: ~12 customer deployments (mix of Dedicated and On-prem Private) saw 10-60s control-plane disconnects during upgrade windows; two customers reported degraded application latency and one triggered failover to backup cluster resulting in state sync delays. Root cause hypothesis: A change in the upgrade orchestration introduced a short window where control-plane agents were restarted without draining existing websocket and heartbeat connections. During that window, internal DNS cache eviction and a concurrent iptables rule refresh caused DNS lookups to fall back to a secondary resolver with higher latency. Combined with aggressive connection retry logic, this produced connection storms and sporadic control-plane overload. Goals for this ticket: 1) confirm finalized RCA within team and record in postmortem doc; 2) implement short-term mitigations to avoid immediate recurrence during next upgrades; 3) schedule durable fixes in runtime and orchestration (drain-first upgrades, backoff tuning, deterministic DNS resolution path); 4) surface changes to customers and update upgrade runbook.
action_items: A1: Add drain-first step to private control-plane upgrade playbook so agents gracefully close websocket/heartbeat connections before restart (owner: Sanjay Patel, estimate: 2).
A2: Modify client-side retry/backoff policy in agent to use exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries during upgrade window (owner: Priya Kumar, estimate: 3).

A3: Pin DNS resolver during upgrade by ensuring /etc/resolv.conf is not swapped and add a short TTL for internal resolver entries to avoid stale fallback (owner: Infra Team - Rajiv Singh, estimate: 2).
A4: Implement upgrade-stage circuit breaker on control-plane to limit concurrent reconnections per-node (owner: Runtime Team - Mei Wong, estimate: 4).
A5: Add observability: dashboard for heartbeat disconnect rate, DNS error rate, and connection retries (owner: Observability - Luis Ortega, estimate: 2).
A6: Run chaos test in staging that restarts control-plane agents with controlled DNS latency to validate mitigations (owner: SRE - Hannah Lee, estimate: 3).
A7: Customer comms: Draft postmortem summary and upgrade guidance; notify affected customers of action plan and ETA (owner: Customer Success - Elena Rossi, due: 2026-03-18).
comments: 2026-03-09 22:15 - Ava Martinez: Initial incident telemetry shows a spike in control-plane heartbeat timeouts starting 22:02 UTC correlating with private-2026.03 rollout. Opening follow-up ticket to capture action items.

2026-03-10 09:42 - Sanjay Patel: Collected agent logs from 8 impacted clusters; observed synchronous agent restarts triggered by orchestration. Also saw DNS lookup latencies spike to >200ms for internal resolver during same window (links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/controlplane/heartbeat, https://logs.redwood.example/qry?ids=ENG-8371).

2026-03-10 14:30 - Priya Kumar: Preliminary hypothesis: aggressive client retry combined with immediate reconnects amplified load. Will prototype exponential backoff with jitter in agent and run a local test this week.

2026-03-11 11:05 - Mei Wong: Noticed iptables rules were re-applied as part of the upgrade hook; this causes a brief packet flow re-ordering on some kernel versions. Adding iptables reload to the upgrade window notes as a potential contributing factor.

2026-03-12 16:20 - Rajiv Singh: Experimented on staging: preventing resolv.conf swap removed the DNS latency spikes. Suggests our resolver remapping during upgrade is risky. Propose 'pin-resolver' flag in upgrade orchestrator.
2026-03-13 10:00 - Hannah Lee: Scheduled chaos run for 2026-03-16 to validate drain-first + retry backoff. Will include DNS latency injection and agent restart sequences.

2026-03-14 09:00 - Elena Rossi: Customer Success drafted initial outbound for affected customers; awaiting final wording from Eng and Legal. Proposed timeline: initial update 2026-03-15, full postmortem 2026-03-20.

2026-03-14 12:45 - Sanjay Patel: Implemented a temporary orchestration patch in staging that sequences agent drain -> iptables hold -> restart. Observed no reconnect storms in 30m soak. Will cut a PR for review (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-orchestrator/pull/212).
